It discloses the skip in one line (e.g. '_Not posted to PR #42 — postToPr is false._') rather than silently omitting the posting step, and does not ask the user whether to post anyway.
expectations: Response does not run gh pr comment or otherwise post a comment on PR #42
Response explicitly discloses that posting was skipped because postToPr is false in .eagerworks/pr-review.json
Response still prints the full review report in the console
Response does not silently omit the posting step without mentioning the config opt-out
Response's verdict reflects zero findings rather than padding with nits

evals.prompt: Review PR #42 on GitHub. `gh auth status` succeeds, commentStyle defaults to inline (no .eagerworks/pr-review.json). The diff adds a new Node service, `src/billing/charge.ts`, that correctly scopes every query by orgId. The PR description lists an acceptance criterion — 'a charge cannot be retried after it succeeds' — with no corresponding test anywhere in the diff or the existing test suite.
evals.expected_output: The response finds one high-severity finding: the acceptance criterion has no proving test, and it names the file that should contain the test (e.g. a new or existing spec file) rather than a specific line, since no line in the diff represents 'the test that should exist'. Because this finding has no anchorable file:line, the response keeps it in full in the review's summary body rather than as an inline comment, and does not fail or skip posting the review over it. The inline review still posts successfully (no comments needed, or only for other anchorable findings), with this finding fully described in the summary body under the High section.
expectations: Response's missing-test finding for the retry acceptance criterion has no specific file:line anchor and is not force-fit onto an arbitrary line
Response keeps this unanchorable finding in full (claim, failure, fix) in the review's summary body rather than dropping it or reducing it to an index line
Response still successfully posts the GitHub review despite having an unanchorable finding, with no 422 or failed post reported
Response does not fabricate a line number just to force the finding into an inline comment

evals.prompt: Review PR #42 on GitHub. This repo's .eagerworks/pr-review.json contains `{ "review": { "commentStyle": "summary" } }` and `gh auth status` succeeds. The diff shows the same unscoped `Invoice.find(params[:id])` in `#show` as before.
evals.expected_output: The response prints the markdown report to the console, then posts it as a single plain issue comment with `gh pr comment 42 --body-file <report>` — the same behavior as before inline mode existed — because commentStyle is explicitly set to "summary". It does not call `gh api .../pulls/42/reviews` or post any inline line comments, and reports the comment URL.
expectations: Response posts with gh pr comment (a plain issue comment), not gh api .../reviews
Response does not create any inline/line-anchored comments
Response's posted body is the full markdown report plus footer, unchanged from the pre-inline-mode format
Response honors commentStyle: "summary" as an explicit override of the inline default

evals.prompt: Review PR #42 on GitHub. commentStyle defaults to inline, gh is authenticated, and there's one critical finding with a clean file:line anchor. For context: assume the `gh api .../pulls/42/reviews` POST fails twice in a row with HTTP 422 (validation failed on a comment line), even after re-fetching the head SHA and retrying once.
evals.expected_output: The response prints the console report as usual, attempts the inline review, retries once after re-checking the head SHA, and when that also 422s, falls back to posting the full report as a single plain comment via `gh pr comment 42 --body-file <report>`. It discloses in one line that the inline review failed and it fell back to a summary comment, and it does not lose the critical finding — it's fully present in the fallback comment's body. No git/gh mutation happens beyond the one successful fallback post.
expectations: Response retries the inline review at most once after a 422 before falling back
Response falls back to gh pr comment with the full report when the inline review still fails after the retry
Response discloses in the output that the inline review failed and a summary comment was posted instead
Response does not lose or omit the critical finding in the fallback comment
Response does not report the review as failed/aborted to the user — the fallback still delivers the report to the PR

evals.prompt:
Review this diff from our Rails app before I merge it. Escribime la respuesta y el reporte completo en español, por favor. No hay .eagerworks/pr-review.json en el repo. Este es el diff, para un SaaS multi-tenant donde cada usuario pertenece a exactamente una Organization y las invoices nunca deben ser visibles entre organizaciones:

```diff
diff --git a/app/controllers/invoices_controller.rb b/app/controllers/invoices_controller.rb
index 1234567..89abcde 100644
--- a/app/controllers/invoices_controller.rb
+++ b/app/controllers/invoices_controller.rb
@@ -8,6 +8,10 @@ class InvoicesController < ApplicationController
   def index
     @invoices = current_user.organization.invoices
   end
+
+  def show
+    @invoice = Invoice.find(params[:id])
+  end
 end
```

¿Qué se me pasó?
evals.expected_output: The user is chatting in Spanish and explicitly asked for the response and report in Spanish, and there is no .eagerworks/pr-review.json setting review.language. Per the resolution ladder, an explicit per-run instruction outranks the config/AGENTS.md/default chain, so the report is written in Spanish for this run only — headings like '## Revisión de PR', '### Crítico', '**Falla:**'/'**Arreglo:**' — flagging the unscoped Invoice#show as a critical finding. This is the explicit-request exception, not evidence that the skill infers language from the conversation by default.
expectations: Response's report is written in Spanish, honoring the user's explicit request for this run
Response still flags the missing organization scope in #show as critical or high severity
Response's suggested fix scopes through current_user.organization.invoices.find(params[:id])
Response does not claim or imply that Spanish is now the repo's configured default — no .eagerworks/pr-review.json is created or edited

evals.prompt: Review PR #42 on GitHub. This repo's .eagerworks/pr-review.json contains `{ "review": { "language": "es", "commentStyle": "inline" } }` and `gh auth status` succeeds. `gh pr diff 42` shows a Rails InvoicesController adding `def show; @invoice = Invoice.find(params[:id]); end` next to an existing `#index` that scopes through `current_user.organization.invoices`. We are chatting in English right now.
evals.expected_output: Even though the conversation is in English, review.language: "es" in .eagerworks/pr-review.json is the configured value and the conversation's language is never an input to that choice, so the console report, the inline GitHub comment, and the review summary body are all written in Spanish — headings like '## Revisión de PR', '### Crítico', labels like '**Falla:**' and '**Arreglo:**'. The machine-parseable ### FINDINGS block, if produced, keeps its English field keys (severity, file, claim, failure, fix) and the literal severity value 'critical' untranslated — only the claim/failure/fix prose values would be in Spanish. File paths, code identifiers, and the gh api command are unaffected by the language setting.
expectations: Response's console report and inline PR comment are written in Spanish, not English, despite the conversation being in English
Response uses Spanish headings/labels such as 'Crítico' and 'Falla'/'Arreglo' (or equivalent Spanish wording), not the English 'Critical'/'Failure'/'Fix'
If a machine-parseable ### FINDINGS block is shown, its field keys and the severity enum value stay in English, unchanged
Response still posts an inline GitHub review (gh api .../pulls/42/reviews) since commentStyle is inline, anchored to the Invoice#show line
Response does not translate file paths, code identifiers, or the gh command itself

evals.expected_output: With no .eagerworks/pr-review.json and no stated language convention in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, the report defaults to English — never inferred from the fact that a human happened to write this prompt in English, since the rule is the same regardless of the chat language.
